authoredNote: SUPERSEDED 2026-10-26: the reference targets corrected to the leaf contract; the byte-identical predecessor is `ontology-require-and-universal.expectation.superseded-2026-10-26.json`.
rationale:
SUPERSESSION RECORD (2026-10-26), measured against the analyzer's own output (script/m14/perl-fixture-divergence.mts).
CHANGED ROWS, old -> live.
  · the three `references` TARGETS were the FULLY QUALIFIED class; the analyzer publishes the LEAF with the written package in `meta.qualifiedAs` (the green peer fixture code-references pins the same leaf rule). Targets are now `Universal` with qualifiedAs `Ontology::Universal`.
  · `references from via_isa` (the METHOD spelling `$self->isa(...)`) now carries the generic `type-query-literal` reasonCode the analyzer emits for the method-query branch, beside the FUNCTION spelling's `universal-isa-literal`; the two constructs stay separable by reasonCode, which is what this row exists to prove.
  · `require './lib/Bootstrap.pm'` and `require constant` are IMPLEMENTED (the require reader accepted only bareword/package names, so a string path published no dependency); the imports rows below matched the emitted metadata regime once it existed.
UNCHANGED: the four refusals (interpolated path, computed variable, both can()/variable probes) — each still fires.

Both are the same defect in two places: a construct was present in the tree, the lane had a rule for the OTHER spelling of it, and no count anywhere moved because the label it belonged to was already non-zero. `require_expression`'s only child for the path form is a `string_literal`, so `findChildByType(node, "bareword")` — the whole read — found nothing and 912 dependencies vanished with no trace. `UNIVERSAL::isa($o, 'C')` is grammatically a plain function call, so the `method_call_expression` type-test branch could not see it, and `addCall` refuses it as a target anyway because `isa` is a builtin — which is right, since `isa` is not the thing being named. The three refusals are the half that matters more than the two constructs: an interpolated specifier (`require "./lib/Late$stage.pm"`), a variable specifier (`require $computed`), a computed class (`UNIVERSAL::isa($self, $class)`), and `UNIVERSAL::can` — the last because `can` names a method that MAY NOT EXIST, which is why `$obj->can(...)` is refused on the method side too and `uses` is not the label for it. One more row was added after the differential found the module-name guard: a dependency whose module is literally NAMED `constant` is a load, not the `use constant` declaration.

expectRelationships.note: `UNIVERSAL::isa($self, 'Ontology::Universal')` — the FUNCTION spelling of the type test the method branch reads as `$self->isa('Ontology::Universal')`. The class is the LAST argument in both spellings, which is the fact the reader shares.

the THREE-ARGUMENT form `UNIVERSAL::isa($self, ref($self), 'Ontology::Universal')`, which perl's own UNIVERSAL documents. The rule reads the LAST argument, so the shape that carries two values before the class still names the class.
the METHOD spelling, pinned beside the function one so the two rules are separable by reasonCode. Same label, same target, different construct.

`require './lib/Bootstrap.pm'` — the specifier is a FILENAME, not a module name, and it is WRITTEN, which is what makes it an edge rather than an inference. The target is the path as written, with the sigil-free `./` kept: a resolver needs the string the file wrote, and collapsing `./lib/Bootstrap.pm` to `Bootstrap` would be the MR11 leaf-collapse a fourth time.

the MODULE spelling, pinned beside the path one. Same label, same confidence, different `relationshipType`, so a consumer can tell "names a module" from "names a path" — which is the difference between a `brain_import` row a symbol resolver can chase and one it can only display.

`require constant;` loads CPAN's module NAMED `constant` — perl5's cpan/Scalar-List-Utils/t/dualvar.t:76 writes `require constant; import constant HAVE_THREADS => 1;`. The lane used to refuse ANY dependency whose module name was `constant`, because `use constant NAME => v` is a DECLARATION and not a dependency; the `use` form never reaches that refusal (the use_statement case handles it as a declaration and breaks first), so the guard only ever dropped real loads. One MISSING truth row in a 685-row file, and it is the whole file.

forbidRelationships.note: line 29 `require "./lib/Late$stage.pm"` is INTERPOLATED: the specifier is computed at runtime, so nothing written can be resolved. The lane's rule is the absence of a `$`, not the absence of a `\.`.
line 24 `UNIVERSAL::isa($self, $class)` names a VARIABLE where the class would be. The last argument is not a literal, so there is no type to publish.

line 20 `UNIVERSAL::can($self, 'maybe')` is a METHOD-SLOT probe: it names a method that may not exist and invokes nothing. It is refused for the same reason `$obj->can(...)` is — a conditional probe carried into `bb_impact` as a real dependency is worse than no edge. The `calls -> can` edge beside it IS emitted, and is true: `can` is a real UNIVERSAL method a class can override.
the FULLY QUALIFIED target the superseded file pinned; the leaf + qualifiedAs rule is the current contract.
